images.alt_grc: ὁ Σωκράτης ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ τοῖς πολίταις διαλέγεται· ὁ δὲ Χαιρεφῶν ἀκούει.
images.alt_en: The Athenian Agora in the morning: Socrates, barefoot, snub-nosed, in a plain cloak, talks with a group of citizens under a plane tree; his thin, excitable friend Chaerephon listens beside him, leaning forward.

images.alt_grc: ἡ Πυθία ἐπὶ τοῦ τρίποδος καθημένη τῷ Χαιρεφῶντι ἀναιρεῖ.
images.alt_en: Inside the temple of Apollo at Delphi: the Pythia, a woman in a white robe and laurel wreath, sits on a tall bronze tripod holding a laurel sprig and a shallow bowl; Chaerephon stands before her, asking his question.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Σωκράτης τὸν πολιτικὸν ἐλέγχει· οἱ δὲ παρόντες ὀργίζονται.
images.alt_en: In a colonnade of the Agora Socrates questions a well-dressed politician, who looks flustered; the politician's friends glare at Socrates, while young men behind him grin.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Αἰγεὺς τὸν θεὸν ἐν Δελφοῖς ἐρωτᾷ.
images.alt_en: Attic red-figure cup by the Kodros Painter, c. 440–430 BC (Berlin, Antikensammlung F 2538): King Aegeus consults the Delphic prophetess, labelled Themis, who sits on Apollo's tripod (museum object, photograph CC).
